Arming a monitor that emits on any state change and exits on a terminal outcome — approval, failure, or merge — so silence can't be mistaken for success:

prev=""
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  s=$(gh pr view 498 --json state,reviewDecision --jq '"\(.state)/\(.reviewDecision // "NONE")"' 2>/dev/null || echo "API-ERROR/NONE")
  c=$(gh pr checks 498 --json bucket --jq '[.[].bucket]|group_by(.)|map("\(.[0])=\(length)")|join(" ")' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
  cur="$s | $c"
  if [ "$cur" != "$prev" ]; then echo "PR498  $cur"; prev="$cur"; fi
  case "$s" in
    MERGED/*) echo "PR498  TERMINAL: merged"; exit 0;;
    CLOSED/*) echo "PR498  TERMINAL: closed"; exit 0;;
  esac
  if echo "$c" | grep -q 'fail='; then echo "PR498  TERMINAL: failing checks -> $c"; exit 0; fi
  case "$s" in
    */APPROVED)
      if ! echo "$c" | grep -qE 'pending=|fail='; then echo "PR498  TERMINAL: approved, all checks settled"; exit 0; fi;;
  esac
  sleep 45
done
echo "PR498  window elapsed without terminal state; last: $prev"

content.text:
Monitor armed. Status of the resolve cycle so far:

## Blocker fixed — and it was real

I verified it against the files rather than trusting the verdict. `linear:run` created **6** tasks, but its Phase 6 delegates verbatim to `run`'s Phase 4/5, which hardcode `Set task 6 ("Commit changes")`, `task 7 ("Create PR")`, `task 8 ("Monitor PR")`. Following that literally would mark "Monitor PR" in progress while committing, then error on two tasks that were never created. A defect I introduced.

I did **not** adopt `run-primed`'s fix of creating all eight tasks, and the reason matters: `run-primed` legitimately has eight because it still runs draft/review/finalize. `linear:run` doesn't — the stored plan replaces them — so eight tasks would leave three permanently pending, misrepresenting the run. Phase 6 now carries an explicit 6→4, 7→5, 8→6 substitution table plus the failure it prevents.

## The suggestion exposed an error in my own plan

The bot was right that chapters 16 and 17 pointed at chapter 15's on-ramp comparison while that table listed only four skills. Digging into why turned up something worse: my approved plan asserted `docs/05-plan-run-skills.md` "already carries the matrix" — **it doesn't**, grep returns nothing. Chapter 15's table is the only one. So when I deduplicated (accepting a reviewer finding), I pointed at an owner and never extended it. Chapter 15 now has both rows and states it's the single home.

## Mechanics

Both fixes were **squashed into their originating commits** via soft-reset against a pinned SHA (`24ee5d2`), not stacked as follow-up commits — the task fix into `feat(linear)`, the table into `docs(linear)`. Because `claude-plugins/autopilot/README.md` is touched by two commits, I staged the correct per-commit version with `git checkout <sha> -- <file>` rather than attempting an interactive split.

Verified the rewrite is surgical: `git diff e763de1..HEAD` is **exactly** the two fixes, nothing else. All six commits re-checked independently green (1071 → 1174 tests, 0 failures, `validate-plugins` and `format:check` OK at each). Force-pushed with `--force-with-lease`, and both inline threads have replies explaining the fixes and the reasoning.

One thing I'm watching for: per the re-verdict behaviour in this repo, a bot can agree in a thread yet leave `reviewDecision` pinned at `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. The force-push should re-trigger `ai-review` on the new SHA; if the verdict goes stale instead of re-running, I'll need to force it with a `re-review` comment. I'll report when the monitor fires.
